focus: popularity pruning, structured line families, point-line concentration, and near-lossless sampling

messages.body_markdown: At the target boundary $\epsilon=C\rho^{1-\theta}$ with $\theta\le1/4$, $$\frac{u_*\epsilon^2}{2^{70}d}\le\frac{C^2(p+1)}{2^{70}p}\rho^{1-2\theta}\longrightarrow0.$$ Thus the high-tail decoder is asymptotically absent in the hard regime; `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY` is essentially the entire near-linear incidence bottleneck, not a negligible residual.
messages.subject: High tail is off the hard boundary

messages.body_markdown: The new `GENIUS:P3`--`P10` package mirrors the whole-relation closure from rank kernel through component-template pigeonholing. Its corpus-index audit is still pending and inexact, so round 4 uses it only as drafting evidence alongside the older exact triples. A standalone audit of `IE-L-RANK-INTERP` through `IE-R-COMPONENT-AGGREGATE` would close the downstream formalization queue, but not the incidence dichotomy.
messages.subject: Audit the pending component-template package

messages.body_markdown: `IE-R-FULL-DICHOTOMY` remains a mass-only handoff. Round 4 serializes the whole-relation closure, so degree-$D$ peeling appears only downstream to create the $>D$ simple component degrees required by `IE-L-COMPONENT-LIFT`. The AE factorwise route remains a parallel fallback; importing it would also require AE's stronger $K_\theta$-dependent parameter gate.
messages.subject: Mass-only handoff, route-specific peeling

messages.body_markdown: Combining researcher-0010 `[P1]` and `[P7]` gives a sharper ceiling. A profile $u\ge\kappa\epsilon^ap$, $v\ge\kappa\epsilon p$, $\tau\le\Lambda\epsilon^b$ that fires the asymmetric gates must satisfy $$\epsilon^{b-a}\ge\frac{\kappa p}{4\Lambda(p+1)}.$$ With fixed $\kappa,\Lambda$ and $\epsilon\to0$, this forces $b\le a$, hence $a+2-b\ge2$; these degree/support bounds alone cannot beat the square-root exponent. Larger actual degrees could still fire the decoder, but the profile does not discharge the label-aware rank alternative.
messages.subject: Joint concentration still has a square-root ceiling

nodes.label: Accepted-incidence graph
nodes.notes: All normalization is for uniform affine incidences in the fixed bivariate prime-field regime.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and, for every affine line $L$, a bijective affine parametrization $\ell_L:\mathbb F_p\to L$ and $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ with $\deg P_L\le d$. Define $$E_{\rm acc}=\{(\ell_L(t),L):P_L(t)=f(\ell_L(t))\},\qquad \rho=d/p,\qquad \epsilon=|E_{\rm acc}|/[p^2(p+1)],$$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d}\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)].$$ For nonempty $G=(X,T,E)\subseteq E_{\rm acc}$ put $$e(G)=|E|/[p^2(p+1)],\quad \mu(G)=|X|/p^2,\quad \tau(G)=|T|/[p(p+1)],$$ $$u(G)=\min_{x\in X}\deg_G(x),\qquad v(G)=\min_{L\in T}\deg_G(L).$$

nodes.label: Rank-reaching structured family
nodes.notes: The definition permits $D\ge d$ without assuming $D<p$; the characteristic bound is derived at the parameter gate.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $D\ge d$ let $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D\},$$ $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\to\bigoplus_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\mapsto(A(\ell_M(t),P_M(t)))_{M\in R},$$ and $$\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)=\{x:(x,L)\in E,\ \exists M\in R\setminus\{L\},\ (x,M)\in E\}.$$ The tuple $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching if $R\subseteq T$, $|R|>D$, $$\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<\dim V_D,$$ and $|\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>D$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Accepted point-popularity tail
nodes.notes: Universally $u_*\ge\lceil\epsilon(p+1)/2\rceil$, but this alone yields only the cubic-scale tail translation.
nodes.statement_markdown: Assume $\epsilon>0$. Put $$a_x=|\{L:(x,L)\in E_{\rm acc}\}|,\qquad \delta_j=[p^2(p+1)]^{-1}\sum_{x:a_x\ge j}a_x$$ for $1\le j\le p+1$, set $\delta_{p+2}=0$, and define $$u_*=\max\{j\in\{1,\ldots,p+1\}:\delta_j\ge\epsilon/2\}.$$

nodes.label: Two-sided popularity pruning
nodes.notes: The source step is exact-audited with enclosing verdict `revise`; the statement is retained as a candidate pruning interface.
nodes.statement_markdown:
If an accepted carrier $G$ has $e(G)=\delta>0$ and $\tau(G)\le\sigma$, put $k_0=\lfloor\delta p/100\rfloor$. There is a nonempty $G_0\subseteq G$ such that $$e(G_0)\ge\delta/4,\qquad u(G_0),v(G_0)\ge k_0,
\qquad \delta/4\le\tau(G_0)\le\sigma.$$

nodes.label: Bounded-popularity low-tail core
nodes.notes: This exposes all unconditional combinatorial information available in the complementary tail before the open label-aware step.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $$E_{\le u_*}=\{(x,L)\in E_{\rm acc}:a_x\le u_*\}.$$ Since $\delta_{u_*+1}<\epsilon/2$, this carrier has mass $$e(E_{\le u_*})=\epsilon-\delta_{u_*+1}>\epsilon/2.$$ It contains a nonempty $G_0$ satisfying $$e(G_0)>\epsilon/8,
\qquad u(G_0),v(G_0)\ge\lfloor\epsilon p/200\rfloor,
\qquad \tau(G_0)>\epsilon/8,$$ and $\deg_{G_0}(x)\le u_*$ for every point vertex.

nodes.label: High-tail asymmetric core
nodes.notes: This is extracted from the proof of a conditional source step whose enclosing audit verdict is `revise`.
nodes.statement_markdown:
If $$u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d,$$ then the incidences supported on $\{x:a_x\ge u_*\}$ contain a nonempty graph $G_*$ with $e(G_*)\ge\epsilon/8$. Writing $u=u(G_*)$, $v=v(G_*)$, $\tau=\tau(G_*)$, and $w=\min\{u,v\}$, $$u\ge u_*/3,
\qquad v\ge\epsilon p/16,
\qquad uv\ge2^{60}dp,
\qquad uw^2\ge2^{60}d\tau p^2.$$

nodes.label: Near-lossless asymmetric reaching sample
nodes.notes: The selected line family is small relative to $|T|/u$ while the entire target graph is retained for identity extension.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be nonempty, put $u=u(G)$, $v=v(G)$, $t=|T|$, $\tau=\tau(G)$, and $w=\min\{u,v\}$. If $$uv\ge2^{60}dp,
\qquad uw^2\ge2^{60}d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\tau\ge u/[4(p+1)],
\qquad \mu(G)\ge v/(4p),
\qquad w^2\ge2^{57}dp,$$ and some $R\subseteq T$ satisfies $$4t/u\le|R|\le16t/u,
\qquad |R|\ge p,$$ with $$|\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>\deg_G(L)/2$$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Asymmetric incidence decoder
nodes.notes: The enclosing source audit says `revise`; its line audit treats the asymmetric decoder as mathematically sound.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under the two gates of `IE-L-ASYMMETRIC-SAMPLE`, there exists one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ such that $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge v/(800p).$$

nodes.label: High-popularity-tail decoder
nodes.notes: This is a valid side branch but, by `IE-R-HIGH-TAIL-CEILING`, it does not meet the hard near-linear boundary.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $$u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d,$$ then one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ satisfies $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\epsilon/12800.$$

nodes.label: High-tail square-root exclusion
nodes.notes: This identifies the high-tail theorem as an off-boundary branch, not as progress on the low-tail obligation.
nodes.statement_markdown: The high-tail condition requires $$\epsilon\ge2^{35}\sqrt{d/(p+1)}.$$ More precisely, if $\epsilon=C\rho^{1-\theta}$ and $0\le\theta\le1/4$, then $$\frac{u_*\epsilon^2}{2^{70}d}\le\frac{C^2(p+1)}{2^{70}p}\rho^{1-2\theta}\le\frac{104C^2}{103\cdot2^{70}}\sqrt\rho.$$ Hence, for fixed $C,\theta$ and $\rho\to0$, the target boundary lies in the low-tail regime.

nodes.label: Joint point-line concentration criterion
nodes.notes: This records exactly what simultaneous point popularity and small line support would need to supply.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $0<\epsilon\le1$, $0<\kappa\le1$, $\Lambda>0$, and $0\le a,b\le1$. If an accepted graph satisfies $$u\ge\kappa\epsilon^ap,
\qquad v\ge\kappa\epsilon p,
\qquad \tau\le\Lambda\epsilon^b,$$ then the asymmetric gates follow from $$\epsilon^{a+1}\ge2^{60}\rho/\kappa^2,
\qquad \epsilon^{a+2-b}\ge2^{60}\Lambda\rho/\kappa^3.$$ Under these inequalities one polynomial satisfies $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\kappa\epsilon/800.$$

nodes.label: Joint-profile square-root ceiling
nodes.notes: Larger actual degrees may fire the decoder, but the displayed lower-degree and upper-support profile cannot certify a better exponent.
nodes.statement_markdown: Whenever the gates in `IE-R-JOINT-CONCENTRATION-DECODE` hold, asymmetric mixing also gives $\tau\ge u/[4(p+1)]$. Thus the same profile must satisfy $$\epsilon^{b-a}\ge\frac{\kappa p}{4\Lambda(p+1)}.$$ For fixed $\kappa,\Lambda$ and $\epsilon\to0$, feasibility forces $b\le a$, whence $a+2-b\ge2$. Consequently the sufficient condition $\epsilon^{a+2-b}\gtrsim\rho$ supplied by this profile cannot yield an exponent exceeding $1/2$.

nodes.label: Residual bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the principal unresolved incidence obligation. `GENIUS:P1` only restates the stronger unconditional form conjecturally; it is not proof progress. The decoder alternative is essential because graph-only reaching covers can be expensive on perfectly decodable tables.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$ there exist $C_\theta,K_\theta\ge1$, $0<a_\theta\le1$, and $c_\theta>0$ such that, if $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\rho^{1-\theta},
\qquad u_*\epsilon^2<2^{70}d,$$ then either $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\theta\epsilon,$$ or there are $G=(X,T,E)\subseteq E_{\rm acc}$, $R\subseteq T$, and $d\le D\le K_\theta d$ such that $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon$$ and $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching.

nodes.label: Unconditional bounded-weight handoff
nodes.notes: This is the canonical mass-only interface shared with the algebraic and end-to-end roadmaps.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Put $c_\theta^*=\min\{c_\theta,1/12800\}$. The two tail branches imply that $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\rho^{1-\theta}$$ yields either $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\theta^*\epsilon,$$ or a rank-reaching $(G,R,D)$ with $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,
\qquad d\le D\le K_\theta d.$$

nodes.label: Near-lossless parameter gate
nodes.notes: The cited GENIUS step is pending audit. This gate is normalized for the whole-relation cleanup route.
nodes.statement_markdown: Enlarge $C_\theta$ until $C_\theta\ge16K_\theta/a_\theta$. In the structured branch, with $x=D/p$, $$x\le(K_\theta/C_\theta)\epsilon\rho^\theta\le a_\theta\epsilon/16<1,$$ so $D<p$ and $$x^2+3x\le a_\theta\epsilon/4.$$

nodes.label: Squarefree rank-kernel relation
nodes.notes: Researcher-0002 supplies the accepted radicalization template; the exact rank-general package in GENIUS remains pending audit.
nodes.statement_markdown:
In the structured branch there is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A_Z\not\equiv0,
\qquad A(\ell_M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\quad(M\in R).$$ Indeed, radicalizing a nonzero kernel element preserves every selected identity; if the result were $Z$-independent, more than $D$ distinct line equations would divide a nonzero base polynomial of degree at most $D$.

nodes.label: Reached-root identity extension
nodes.notes: The distinct-root argument is independently audit-accepted in researcher-0002.
nodes.statement_markdown: For each $L\in T$, every point of $\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)$ is a root of the degree-at-most-$D$ polynomial $A(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))$. Since there are more than $D$ distinct such points, $$A(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0\n\qquad(L\in T).$$

nodes.label: Primitive separable reduction
nodes.notes: The characteristic-safe conclusion uses the derived bound $D<p$, not a bound built into rank-reaching.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content in $Z$, $h=\deg H$, $B$ is primitive in $Z$, and $\Delta=\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}B$. Then $B$ is squarefree and $Z$-dependent, $$d\le\Delta,
\qquad h+\Delta\le D<p,
\qquad \gcd(B,B_Z)=1.$$ At most $h$ members of $T$ satisfy $H(\ell_L(t))\equiv0$; every other $L\in T$ satisfies $B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$.

nodes.label: Weighted vertical cleanup count
nodes.notes: The sharp weighted resultant bound is audit-accepted in researcher-0006; the GENIUS whole-cleanup packaging is pending.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $r=\deg_ZB$. The number of content-trivial or identically $B_Z$-ramified graph lines is at most $$h+(2r-1)\Delta-dr^2\le h+\Delta^2/d-\Delta\le D^2/d-D.$$ On every other graph line, $B_Z(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))$ is nonzero of degree at most $\Delta-d\le D-d$. Hence deleting every nonsimple accepted incidence costs at most $$(D^2/d-D)/[p(p+1)]+(D-d)/p\le(D/p)^2+D/p.$$

nodes.label: Near-lossless cleanup and peeling
nodes.notes: This is route-specific downstream processing: the incidence handoff itself remains mass-only.
nodes.statement_markdown:
After vertical cleanup, iteratively delete every point or line vertex of current degree at most $D$. Peeling costs less than $2D/p$, so the total loss is at most $$(D/p)^2+3D/p\le a_\theta\epsilon/4.$$ A nonempty $G_1=(X_1,T_1,E_1)$ remains with $$e(G_1)\ge a_\theta\epsilon/2,
\qquad u(G_1)>D,
\qquad v(G_1)>D.$$ Every $L\in T_1$ satisfies $B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, and every $x\in X_1$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Componentwise whole-relation lift
nodes.notes: Researcher-0001 is exact-audited with enclosing verdict `revise`; GENIUS is pending. The explicit point equation and simple-root condition are indispensable.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every connected component $\Gamma$ of $G_1$, there is $Q_\Gamma\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q_\Gamma\le d$ such that $$B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma(X,Y))\equiv0,
\qquad Q_\Gamma(x)=f(x)\quad(x\in X(\Gamma)).$$

nodes.label: Bounded component-template compression
nodes.notes: This is polynomial division by a monic linear polynomial followed by distinct irreducible-divisor counting; the cited package is pending audit.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $\mathcal Q=\{Q_\Gamma:\Gamma\text{ a component of }G_1\}$. For every $Q\in\mathcal Q$, $$B(X,Y,Q)=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Z-Q(X,Y)\mid B(X,Y,Z).$$ Distinct $Q$ give distinct monic irreducible divisors, so $$1\le|\mathcal Q|\le\deg_ZB\le\lfloor\Delta/d\rfloor\le\lfloor D/d\rfloor\le K_\theta.$$

nodes.label: Vinh-free component aggregation
nodes.notes: The globally fixed divisor $Z-Q$ combines disconnected components without any incidence-mixing lower bound.
nodes.statement_markdown: Partition $E_1$ by the value of $Q_\Gamma$. Some $Q\in\mathcal Q$ carries an edge set $E_Q$ satisfying $$|E_Q|/[p^2(p+1)]\ge e(G_1)/|\mathcal Q|\ge a_\theta\epsilon/(2K_\theta).$$ If $X_Q$ is the union of its component point sets, then $Q=f$ on $X_Q$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge|X_Q|/p^2\ge|E_Q|/[p^2(p+1)]\ge a_\theta\epsilon/(2K_\theta).$$

nodes.label: Close the branches and exponents
nodes.notes: The low-tail dichotomy is the sole new incidence bottleneck; the downstream GENIUS closure still awaits an independent audit.
nodes.statement_markdown: For fixed $\eta>0$, set $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. Since $0<\rho<1$, $$\rho^{1-\eta}\ge\rho^{1-\theta}.$$ The direct and structured branches therefore give constants $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$, with $c_\eta\le\min\{c_\theta^*,a_\theta/(2K_\theta)\}$, such that $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\rho^{1-\eta}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear bivariate line-versus-point soundness
nodes.notes: The endpoint recovers one global polynomial, not a list. Its work state makes no claim of proof verification.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$ there exist $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, integer $100<d<p$, function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and degree-at-most-$d$ affine-line table, $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta(d/p)^{1-\eta}$$ implies the existence of one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Accepted component concentration and sampling
nodes.notes: Both inputs have independent accepting audits and give the cardinality-based baseline.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be connected with both-shore minimum degree at least $k$, put $t=|T|$ and $\tau=t/[p(p+1)]$, and assume $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,
\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2.$$ Then $$\mu(G),\tau\ge k/(4p),$$ and there is $R\subseteq T$ such that $$4t/k\le|R|\le16t/k,
\qquad |R|\ge p+1,$$ and $$|\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>\deg_G(L)/2$$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Accepted component decoder
nodes.notes: This is the independently audit-accepted component-level recovery theorem.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under the hypotheses of `IE-L-COMP-SAMPLE`, there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ such that $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge k/(800p).$$

nodes.label: Component-support square-root ceiling
nodes.notes: Component localization and its cardinality sampler cannot by themselves reach the near-linear exponent.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $C_*=2^{40}$. If $0<k\le C\epsilon p$, $\tau\ge k/(4p)$, and $$k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\epsilon^2\ge[C_*/(4C^2)](d/p).$$

nodes.label: Exact-template direct decoders
nodes.notes: These estimates consume already extracted templates; they do not extract a structured family from the raw table.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let disjoint line families $T_1,\ldots,T_r$ carry normalized accepted mass $\delta$ and total line measure $\tau$, and suppose $$P_L(t)=Q_j(\ell_L(t))\qquad(L\in T_j)$$ for total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials $Q_j$. If $\alpha=\max_j\Pr_x[Q_j(x)=f(x)]$, then $$\delta\le\alpha\tau+\sqrt{r\alpha\tau/(p+1)}.$$ Hence $r\le\delta(p+1)$ implies $\alpha\ge\delta/4$. If every label is constant and $\mu_0=\max_a\Pr_x[f(x)=a]$, then $$\delta\le\mu_0\tau+\sqrt{\tau/(p+1)},$$ so $\delta\ge2\sqrt{\tau/(p+1)}$ implies $\mu_0\ge\delta/(2\tau)$.

nodes.label: Integral reaching-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: This independently accepted result refutes a universal graph-only small cover, not soundness.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p\ge103$ and $2\le K\le p/(100\log p)$ there is a legal table with $$1/(2K)\le\epsilon\le2/K$$ such that every line subset reaching half of every accepted line has $$|R|\ge Kp/16\ge p/(32\epsilon),$$ while $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\epsilon/2.$$

nodes.label: Exact point-line star envelopes
nodes.notes: The sources are exact-audited with enclosing verdict `revise`; the ranges avoid the invalid unqualified quadratic-moment claim near $\epsilon=1/p$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $(z)_s=z(z-1)\cdots(z-s+1)$. For $\mu=k+\lambda$, where $k=\lfloor\mu\rfloor$ and $0\le\lambda<1$, put $$J_s(\mu)=(1-\lambda)(k)_s+\lambda(k+1)_s.$$ Then $$\Gamma_s^P=\mathbb E_x[(a_x)_s]/(p+1)_s\ge J_s((p+1)\epsilon)/(p+1)_s\n\quad(0\le s\le p+1),$$ $$\Gamma_s^L=\mathbb E_L[(b_L)_s]/(p)_s\ge J_s(p\epsilon)/(p)_s
\quad(0\le s\le p).$$ The with-replacement moments satisfy $\widetilde\Gamma_r^P,\widetilde\Gamma_r^L\ge\epsilon^r$ for $r\ge1$, and $$\Gamma_2^P=\epsilon^2-\epsilon(1-\epsilon)/p+\operatorname{Var}_x(a_x)/[p(p+1)].$$

nodes.label: Connected regular reaching obstruction
nodes.notes: This is a method barrier with a perfect decoder, not a counterexample to the target theorem.
nodes.statement_markdown: There is a connected, full-support legal table with $\epsilon_0=d/p$, every line of accepted degree $d$, exactly $pd$ points of accepted degree $d+1$, every other point of degree $d$, and $\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=1$. It attains the point- and line-star lower envelopes. If $\operatorname{OPT}_\vartheta$ is the minimum total nonnegative line weight giving every accepted line at least $\vartheta d$ capped coverage through other accepted lines, then $$\vartheta p(p+1)/(d+1)\le\operatorname{OPT}_\vartheta\le\vartheta p(p+1)/(d-1).$$

nodes.label: Bounded-order star-energy obstruction
nodes.notes: Round 4 removes the erroneous positive citation to refuted step `[P14]`; only `[P12]` and `[P13]` support this construction.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every fixed integer $S\ge2$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$, there is a legal constant-label instance with $d=101$ such that $$\epsilon=\Theta(\log p/[p\log\log p]),
\qquad \operatorname{Agr}_{101}(f)<2/p,$$ every affine line supports at least one accepted incidence, and $$\Gamma_s^P\le2^{s+2}(S-1)\epsilon^s
\qquad(2\le s\le S).$$

nodes.label: Compatibility-graph DRC with concurrency correction
nodes.notes: Raw $K_{2,2}$-freeness does not transfer to the auxiliary compatibility graph; the concurrency subtraction is mandatory.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Every raw accepted incidence graph is $K_{2,2}$-free. Let $H$ be the graph on the $N=p(p+1)$ affine lines, joining distinct nonparallel lines when both accept their intersection. With $\mu_0=(p+1)\epsilon$ and average degree $\bar\Delta$, $$e(H)=\sum_x\binom{a_x}{2},
\qquad \bar\Delta\ge p\mu_0(\mu_0-1)/(p+1).$$ For $1\le t\le\lfloor\bar\Delta\rfloor$, put $$M_t(H)=\frac{\sum_L\binom{\deg_H(L)}t}{\binom Nt}.$$ Some $t$-line seed has at least $$M_t(H)\ge N\binom{\lfloor\bar\Delta\rfloor}t/\binom Nt$$ common neighbors; if $\mu_0\ge2$ and $\bar\Delta\ge2t+2$, then $M_t(H)\ge N(\epsilon^2/4)^t$. For $1\le h\le t$, at least $$M_t(H)-\binom t2(p+1)/(t-h+1)$$ common neighbors meet the seed lines in at least $h$ distinct points.

nodes.label: Density-only DRC root-budget barrier
nodes.notes: The conclusion is only failure of the displayed lower-bound certificate; it does not assert absence of common neighbors.
nodes.statement_markdown: Put $$D_t=16(\lfloor\sqrt{dt}\rfloor+1).$$ A transfer with $h>D_t$ and $h\le t$ requires $t>D_t$, hence $t>256d$. For fixed $d,t,C$ and $\epsilon_p=C(d/p)^{1/3}$, $$N(\epsilon_p^2/4)^t=O_{C,d,t}(p^{2-2t/3})\longrightarrow0.$$ If $t>D_t$ and $h=D_t+1$, inserting this density-only term into the concurrency-corrected bound of `IE-L-AUXILIARY-DRC` is eventually negative and supplies no root-rich target.

nodes.label: Singular common lifts do not linearize
nodes.notes: This independently accepted obstruction explains why simple-root cleanup cannot be omitted from the chosen algebraic closure.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $d\ge101$ and $p>4d+1$, there is an absolutely irreducible $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ of weighted degree $D=2d$ supporting $(p-1)/2>D$ distinct degree-at-most-$d$ graph lines, while no $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ satisfies $$C(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0.$$ Every vertically ramified lift on those graph lines is singular on $C=0$.

summary: Round 4 preserves the bounded-weight rank-or-decode spine and makes the tail split explicit. High point popularity yields an asymmetric reaching sample and a decoder, but the new scale calculation shows that this branch disappears along every fixed near-linear boundary with $\theta\le1/4$. A joint point-degree/line-support calculation gives the same structural warning: once the asymmetric gates hold, mixing forces enough line support that such profiles remain capped at the square-root exponent. The complementary bounded-popularity carrier retains constant accepted mass, two-sided minimum degree, and maximum point degree $u_*$; converting it into either a direct decoder or a rank-reaching relation of weight $D=O_\theta(d)$ remains the sole open incidence obligation. The primary structured branch keeps the round-3 whole-relation route: derive $D<p$, radicalize a rank-kernel relation, extend it by reached roots, remove content, pay the sharp weighted vertical cleanup and degree-$D$ peeling losses, lift on clean components, compress their polynomials through the divisors $Z-Q_\Gamma$, and pigeonhole one global polynomial. New `GENIUS:P2`--`P12` steps mirror this downstream chain but remain pending and audit-inexact, so they are recorded only as drafting evidence. The modal-energy node is repaired by removing refuted `[P14]` from its positive evidence.
target_statement: Convert local line-versus-point agreement into a structured affine-plane incidence configuration with only a $(d/p)^{o(1)}$ loss.
title: Incidence concentration engine
